data/0/entries/6/entries/3/entries/3/ent.english: Chultans in Port Nyanzaru seldom don armor because of the climate, but large, colorful shields made from toughened dinosaur hide are ubiquitous. These shields are called hlang and function as ordinary shields. In melee, they favor the traditional {@item yklwa|ToA} (pronounced YICK-ul-wah), a short, broad-bladed, one-handed, spear-like weapon. For more information about the yklwa, see "{@area Buying a Special Item|084|x}."

data/0/entries/6/entries/3/entries/8/ent.english: Some Chultan guides are aware of one grung village due south of Port Nyanzaru, just above the headwater of the River Tiryki (pronounced tee-REE-kee). For more information on this village, see "{@area Dungrunglung|0d8|x}." {@adventure Appendix D|ToA|9|Grungs} contains additional information on grungs.

data/1/entries/1.english: Port Nyanzaru hugs the coastline at the south end of the Bay of Chult. No other city exists in Chult, along the coast or anywhere else, except in ruins or overrun by monstrous creatures. Until recently, Port Nyanzaru was under the firm control of Amn, a foreign nation. Nine years ago, Amn was forced to relinquish the city to a wealthy and powerful consortium of Chultan traders backed by the Ytepka Society (pronounced yeh-TEP-kah), or risk a bloody conflict that probably would have ended with the city winning its independence anyway. Seven Chultan traders have since grown into influential merchant princes, enticing folk from up and down the Sword Coast with their wares.

data/1/entries/8/entries/1.english: The city is defined by four steep hills. The westernmost hill, called Temple Hill because it's home to the temple of Savras, is completely walled off from lower ground. A wide stone bridge crosses on arched columns from Temple Hill to Throne Hill, site of Goldenthrone. A second bridge connects Throne Hill to the southern slopes, site of several merchant princes' villas. East of the harbor, the Hall of Gold gleams atop the city's tallest hill, Mount Sibasa, which is connected by bridge to the neighboring Yklwazi Hill (pronounced yick-ul-WAH-zee), site of the Grand Coliseum. Steep, stepped streets and terraces surround each hill.

data/1/entries/9/entries/2/entries/9/ent.english: {@creature Kwayothé|ToA} (NE female Chultan human {@creature priest} wearing a {@item ring of fire resistance}) is calm and contemplative in a way that's vaguely menacing. She worships the fire god Kossuth (pronounced kaw-SOOTH) and likes torturing others, particularly if it involves fire and hot coals. Kwayothé has two consorts—a {@creature succubus} named Ixis and an {@creature incubus} named Indar. These fiends take the forms of beautiful Chultans.

data/1/entries/12/entries/2/entries/8/en.english: A yklwa (pronounced YICK-ul-wah) is a simple melee weapon that is the traditional weapon of Chultan warriors. A yklwa consists of a 3-foot wooden shaft with a steel or stone blade up to 18 inches long. It costs 1 gp, and it deals {@dice 1d8} piercing damage on a hit. Although it has the thrown weapon property, the yklwa is not well balanced for throwing (range 10/30 ft.).

data/2/entries/4/entries/10/entries/10/e.english: Four green-skinned {@creature Grung|VGM|grungs} (warriors) emerge from nearby hovels to confront strangers who approach the shrine unescorted. They attack if no one speaks the correct passphrase in Grung ("Roook, roooook, erp"). If a fight breaks out, reinforcements in the form of twelve {@creature Grung|VGM|grungs} arrive in 2 rounds. The grungs in {@area area 3|0dd|x} begin shooting arrows at the same time.

data/2/entries/4/entries/20/entries/13/e.english: {@creature Asharra|ToA} and an elderly female {@creature aarakocra} servant named Yingmatona (pronounced ying-mah-TOE-nah) live in this grand structure. No other aarakocra ever set foot inside. Mwaxanaré visits occasionally, and only {@creature Na|ToA} is allowed to come and go as he pleases. This building is off-limits to the characters unless they're invited inside. Trespassing in the Teacher's home is a horrendous breach of hospitality.

data/2/entries/4/entries/32/entries/0.english: Port Castigliar (pronounced kah-STEE-lee-ar) is a port in name only. In fact, it's nothing more than a stretch of beach with an abandoned supply depot, seven battered huts made of bamboo and thatch, and a defiled graveyard. Undead drove away the inhabitants long ago, and ghouls dug up the graves.

data/3/entries/3/entries/6/entries/6/ent.english: The characters could form an alliance with the Red Wizards to recover the puzzle cube taken by the yuan-ti. If an accord is reached, Zagmira reveals that she has a spy in the yuan-ti temple: a yuan-ti pureblood named Ishmakahl (pronounced ISH-mah-kawl). Zagmira doesn't reveal that this spy is a doppelganger.

data/3/entries/4/entries/17/entries/5/en.english: When a character enters this chamber, give the players a copy of handout 16 in {@adventure appendix E|ToA|10}. This grid is a puzzle key. If the letters from the riddle in area 16C are entered into the grid (minus spaces), the letters in the darkened squares spell out "cover eyes." This phrase provides a clue to obtaining the puzzle cube in area 16C.

data/4/entries/4/entries/2/entries/3.english: A {@creature Yuan-ti Malison (Type 1)||type 1 yuan-ti malison} named Nahth (pronounced NAWTH) and four {@creature Yuan-ti Broodguard|VGM|yuan-ti broodguards} (see {@adventure appendix D|ToA|9}) defend the main gate. Strangers are denied entry unless they are accompanied by one or more yuan-ti.

data/4/entries/4/entries/3/entries/1.english: Yuan-ti troops muster in this hall before heading into the city. Unless they have been drawn elsewhere, a {@creature yuan-ti pureblood} named Soakosh (pronounced SOH-kawsh) and four {@creature Yuan-ti Broodguard|VGM|yuan-ti broodguards} (see {@adventure appendix D|ToA|9}) are stationed here. Two {@creature Basilisk||basilisks} chained to hooks in the western alcoves are trained not to look their yuan-ti masters in the eye. Chewed bits of stone (the remains of {@condition petrified} victims) litter the floor in the alcoves. The {@creature triceratops} confined to the metal pen in the northwest corner is docile until threatened. The yuan-ti use it to pull supply wagons.

data/4/entries/4/entries/5/entries/3.english: A {@creature Bone Naga (Spirit)||bone naga} named Ukurlahmu (pronounced oo-ker-LAH-moo) has orders to protect the armory from thieves, but it struggles to remember faces. It only attacks creatures who fail to speak the correct passphrase. The current passphrase is "black mask." Characters are given three chances to utter the correct phrase before Ukurlahmu attacks. Before it attacks, the naga uses a bonus action to speak a magic command word that causes two {@creature Minotaur Skeleton||minotaur skeletons} to rise from the bones on the floor. The skeletons obey the naga.

data/4/entries/4/entries/11/entries/5/en.english: The doppelganger infiltrated the temple by killing and assuming the form of a male yuan-ti pureblood named Ishmakahl (pronounced ISH-mah-kawl). It has been sent by Zagmira, a Red Wizard, to spy on {@creature Ras Nsi|ToA}. Unfortunately for its employers, the doppelganger has had little contact with {@creature Ras Nsi|ToA} since arriving at the fane; however, it has learned a few things by eavesdropping on {@creature Sekelok|ToA} and Neema's intimate conversations.

data/4/entries/4/entries/15/entries/2.english: Yuan-ti use this chamber to extract venom from snakes. Xopal (pronounced zoh-PAUL), a {@creature yuan-ti pureblood}, bottles and blends the venom to create deadly new strains. Five human {@creature Zombie||zombies} serve Xopal as laborers.

data/4/entries/4/entries/18/entries/3.english: Unless they have been fought and defeated elsewhere, two enslaved men (NE male Chultan human {@creature Gladiator||gladiators}) watch Yahru (pronounced YAH-roo), a {@creature Yuan-ti Malison (Type 1)||type 1 yuan-ti malison}, as he sheds his skin (a process that can take up to an hour). Yahru is {@creature Ras Nsi|ToA}'s spymaster, and he doesn't like to be disturbed. Characters passing themselves off as yuan-ti purebloods are instructed to leave the room at once. Enslaved characters are ordered to smear ointment on Yahru's skin to expedite the skin-shedding process.

data/5/entries/3/entries/3/entries/5/ent.english: This jeweled goblet was crafted from the skull of a long-dead Omuan king and served as a symbol of office for the royal line of Omu. The legendary Chultan hero Ch'gakare (pronounced chuh-GAH-kah-ree) is said to have beheaded the king after escaping the Nine Hells on the back of a mastodon.

data/5/entries/6/entries/12/entries/9/en.english: {@creature Withers|ToA} has enough equipment on his desk to assemble a scholar's pack. A {@item manual of golems} (clay) lies open on his desk next to a spellbook containing all the spells he has prepared. On the inside back cover of the spellbook is what appears to be a name: Khomara Blackfire. "Khomara" and "Blackfire" are actually the command words for the {@item mirror of life trapping} in {@area area 50|44c|x}.
data/5/entries/6/entries/12/entries/9/en.reason: 鏡子的啟動口令與法術書線索

data/5/entries/7/entries/18/entries/2/en.english: The {@creature beholder}, Belchorzh (pronounced BEL-korj), floats at the top of the room. {@creature Acererak|ToA} cast a {@spell wish} spell to render Belchorzh {@condition invisible}. A successful {@spell dispel magic} ({@dc 19}) cast on the beholder or contact with an {@spell antimagic field} ends its invisibility. Belchorzh reacts to intruders as described in the "Beholder Tactics" section below.

data/5/entries/8/entries/7/entries/4.english: The mirror has two command words. Speaking the word "Khomara" while standing within 5 feet of the mirror deactivates or reactivates it. (The mirror can't trap creatures while deactivated.) Speaking the word "Blackfire" along with a cell number frees the creature trapped in that cell.
data/5/entries/8/entries/7/entries/4.reason: 鏡子的啟動口令與法術書線索

data/5/entries/9/entries/10/entries/4/en.english: An {@creature aboleth} named G'lyh'rul (guh-LEE-rool) lives in the lake. When {@creature Acererak|ToA} enslaved it, the aboleth lost its mind and developed a split personality. Its dominant aspect awaits the coming of the death god, which it believes heralds the fall of divinity. Until that day, the aboleth humbly obeys {@creature Withers|ToA} (whom the creature refers to by his original name of Gorra) and attacks anyone seeking to prevent the atropal's ascension. The aboleth's other personality is that of a humanoid child—harmless, gleeful, and insanely curious. In this state of mind, the aboleth poses no threat to anyone and flees if attacked. Roll any die to determine which personality is dominant at any given time. On an even result, the aboleth's childlike personality is dominant.

data/5/entries/9/entries/12/entries/2.english: The murals on the walls tell the story of Ch'gakare (pronounced chuh-GAH-kah-ree), a Chultan warrior who stole his king's prized steed: a mastodon named Ghom. As punishment, the king's sorcerers banished Ch'gakare and Ghom to the Nine Hells, but the two fought their way back home. On his return, Ch'gakare chopped off the king's head and turned his skull into a jeweled chalice. Any character who studies the murals and succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}) check recognizes the legend and can recount it. The murals show Ch'gakare and Ghom fighting spined devils, bearded devils, barbed devils, horned devils, and erinyes.

data/5/entries/10/entries/6/entries/1/en.english: A large, cracked, six-sided mirror is mounted above a stone shelf protruding from the opposite wall. Five unlit candles stand on the shelf, each made of yellow wax and covered with tiny black sigils. Scrawled on the wall above the mirror in dried blood are the words "PIGGY PIGGY PIGGY."
data/5/entries/10/entries/6/entries/1/en.reason: 機關啟動用的字面拼寫

data/5/entries/10/entries/6/entries/3/en.english: If all six candles are lit, a character who looks in the mirror and says the word "piggy" three times in a row sees the reflected candlelight reveal a wooden lever set into a metal panel on the north wall. If fewer than six candles are lit when the words are spoken, the lever appears on the south wall instead. These levers exist only in the mirror's reflection, not in reality.

data/5/entries/11/entries/8/entries/0.english: This concludes {@i Tomb of Annihilation}. Space limitations preclude us from exploring Chult in its entirety, but you can create your own Chult-based adventures and publish them at the Dungeon Masters Guild ({@link www.dmsguild.com|https://www.dmsguild.com}).

data/8/entries/1/entries/10/entries/0.english: A yahcha (pronounced YAH-chah) is a harmless, meaty beetle about the size of a human hand, which feeds on worms and maggots. It moves slowly (walking speed 10 feet) and is easy to catch. A creature with {@disease blue mist fever|ToA} that eats a raw or cooked yahcha can immediately make a saving throw with advantage against that disease (see {@adventure "Diseases,"|ToA|2|Diseases} page 40).
